Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Sad

It is Meccan.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Sad﴾. The majority of readers recited ﴿Sad﴾ with sukun (silent final letter). Al-Hasan recited ﴿Sad﴾ with the letter dal in the genitive (kasra), and ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Nahwi (the grammarian) recited ﴿Sad﴾ with the letter dal in the accusative (fatha). The well-known reading is with sukun.

The reason for the sukun is that it is one of the letters of the muqatta'at (disjointed letters, the opening letters of certain surahs), and among the Arabs such a letter is pronounced with sukun. As for the reading of al-Hasan, its meaning is: "Sad the Quran by your deeds," that is, confront it (ʿaraḍa) with your deeds. As for the reading with fatha, its meaning is: "Indeed you are Sad."

As for the meaning of "Sad": it is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "Muhammad spoke the truth." And from al-Dahhak: "Allah spoke the truth." Mujahid said: "This is one of the openings of the surahs." Qatada said: "It is one of the names of the Quran, and it is an oath." Al-Kalbi mentioned that its meaning is: "And by the truthful one," the meaning being that of an oath.

As for His words: ﴿And by the Quran, full of reminder﴾, that is, full of honour (dhi'l-sharaf). He has said elsewhere: ﴿Indeed We have sent down to you a Book in which is your reminder﴾, that is, your honour.

"And His saying: ﴿Nay, but those who disbelieve are in arrogance and opposition﴾. It was recited in the irregular (shadhdh) reading: "fi gharra wa shiqaq" with the dotted ghayn, whereas the well-known reading is with the ʿayn and the zayn.

And His saying: ﴿in arrogance﴾ means: in zealous pride (ḥamiyyah). Qatadah said: the meaning of His saying ﴿ʿizzah﴾ is that they recoiled from accepting the truth and grew proud, refusing to submit. As for the reading with the ghayn, it comes from ghurur (delusion) and ghaflah (heedlessness). And His saying: ﴿wa shiqaq﴾ means: enmity and discord."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 3:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿How many a generation did We destroy before them﴾. Know that the scholars of tafsir differed regarding the response (jawab) to the oath. Some of them said: the response to the oath is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, that is true: the dwellers of the Fire quarrelling﴾ (Q. 38:64). This is a weak view, because many stories and reports have intervened between the oath and this response.

The second view: the response to the oath is His saying ﴿How many a generation did We destroy﴾, and there is an ellipsis in it, and its meaning is: "Indeed, We destroyed..." (la-kam ahlakna).

The third view: the response to the oath is omitted, and its meaning is: "Sad. By the Qur'an, full of reminder, the matter is not as they claim", meaning the disbelievers.

His saying: ﴿How many (kam) a generation did We destroy before them﴾. Kam is used for multiplicity (al-takthir), and "generation" (qarn) has already been explained earlier.

His saying: ﴿Then they cried out﴾, meaning they called for help at the time of destruction. His saying: ﴿but it was no time for escape﴾, meaning it was not a time for flight (firar). It was also said: not a time for refuge (maghab). It is said: they cried out, but it was not a time for crying out.

"Wa-lat" (but not) with the meaning of "laysa" (is not) is a Yemeni dialect usage. It was also said: the "ta'" was joined to "la" for emphasis, just as it is said "rubba" and "thumma" with the meanings of "rubba" and "thumma". The lexicographers said: "naasa" (yanuusu) means to withdraw, and "baasa" (yabuusu) means to advance. The poet said:

(Is it from remembrance of Salma that you withdraw, so that you fall short of her by a step, and then advance?)

Another poet said, using "lat" with the meaning of "laysa":

(They sought reconciliation, but it was no time for it, so we answered that it was not a time for survival.)

Some of them mentioned that it was the custom of the Arabs, when war became fierce, for one of them to say to another: "Manas! Manas!", meaning: charge in one single charge, in which whoever is saved is saved and whoever perishes perishes. They said this when the punishment of God came upon them. So God, may He be exalted, said to them: ﴿but it was no time for escape﴾, meaning: and it was not the time for this saying. One of them recited a line of poetry:

(You remember your love for Layla, but it is no longer the time, and grey hair has come, cutting off the companion.)

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they wonder that a warner has come to them from among themselves﴾, i.e., Muhammad. And His saying: ﴿And the disbelievers say, "This is a sorcerer, a liar"﴾, i.e., a deceiver, a liar.

Tafsir al-Quran of al-Sam'ani, on Surah 38, verse 5:

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Has he made the gods into one God? Indeed, this is a astonishing thing.﴾ That is: "ajab" (marvel). ʿAjīb and ʿujāb carry one meaning. Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Sulami recited: "inna hadha la-shay'un ʿujābun" with the shadda (emphatic doubling), and it has the same meaning as the first.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 6:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And the chiefs among them went forth﴾. The occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul) of this verse is that "the notables of Quraysh came to Abu Talib, namely Abu Jahl, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Utba, Shayba, Tu'ayma ibn 'Adi, 'Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt, Ubayy and Umayya, the two sons of Khalaf, Zam'a ibn al-Aswad, and others. They complained to him about Muhammad, saying: 'He reviles our gods, belittles our minds, and claims that our fathers are in the Fire.' So Abu Talib summoned the Prophet and said: 'O son of my brother, these are your people who have come complaining about you, mentioning such-and-such. What do you want from them?' He said: 'I want from them one word; if they say it, the Arabs will submit to them, and the non-Arabs will pay them the jizya.' The people said: 'We will say ten words. What do you want?' He said: 'Say: There is no god but Allah.' They recoiled and stood up, saying: 'We will never say it, ever.' Some of them said to others: 'Go on, and be steadfast in [the worship of] your gods,' meaning: keep to them, and maintain your worship of them."

And His words: ﴿Indeed, this is a thing that is intended﴾. That is: the matter of Muhammad is a thing, through which evil and destruction are intended for the people. Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, recited: "And the chiefs went forth, walking, [saying]: Be steadfast upon your gods." It is also said: ﴿this is a thing that is intended﴾ means: a thing intended against the people of the earth by the sending of Muhammad. And it is said: "intended" means: intended against Muhammad, and he will rule over us and become our chief.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that it was revealed concerning the conversion of 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, and the strength that came to the Muslims through his presence. So when 'Umar embraced Islam, the disbelievers said: ﴿Indeed, this is a thing that is intended﴾, that is: indeed the matter of Muhammad is a thing intended, since it grew strong through the conversion of 'Umar.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 7:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿We have not heard of this in the last religion﴾ — that is, the Christian (al-Nasraniyyah) religion. This is what Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jurayj and al-Suddi said. It is the last of the religions, and they were not monotheists, for they used to say: "Allah is the third of three." Mujahid said: "We have not heard of this in the last religion" means: in the religion of the Quraysh. It was also said: in our religion, this one. And it is related from Mu'arrij ibn ʿAmr, who said: "In the last religion" means: in the first religion. This is a dialect of some of the Arabs.

And His words: ﴿This is nothing but a fabrication﴾ — that is, a contrivance and a lie.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 8:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Has the Reminder been sent down upon him from among us?﴾ mean: the people of Mecca said, "Has the Qur'an been sent down upon Muhammad (ﷺ) from among us, when he is neither the most excellent of us nor the most noble of us?"

And His words: ﴿Nay, they are in doubt about My Reminder﴾ mean: they are in doubt about what has been sent down.

And His words: ﴿Nay, they have not yet tasted My punishment﴾ mean: they have not yet tasted My punishment, but they will taste it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Or do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord?﴾ Its meaning is: Do they possess the treasuries of the mercy of your Lord? And "khaza'in" (treasuries) are the chambers (buyut) in which precious things are stored.

The real meaning is: they do not possess the treasuries of mercy and prophethood, so that they could give it to whomever they wish and withhold it from whomever they wish.

And His saying: ﴿the Mighty, the Bestower﴾. "Al-'Aziz" (the Mighty) is the one who is unassailable in His dominion, the one who prevails over His creation. "Al-Wahhab" (the Bestower) is the one who gives to His creatures,

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 10:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Or do they have the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them?﴾ That is: they do not have that.

And His saying: ﴿Then let them ascend by the means (asbab)﴾, that is: then let them rise up by means of strength and protection, if that is theirs as they claim. This was said by Abu 'Ubayda. It was also said: then let them sit down at the gates of the heaven. The asbab (means, ways of access) in language are that which connects, and a rope is called a sabab because one is connected by it to a thing. So ascending by the asbab is reaching from one thing to another until one attains its highest point. The purpose of the verse is to establish their incapacity and to nullify their claim regarding the protection and strength they assert.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 11:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿A host of confederates, defeated, will be there﴾, meaning: a host there. "Ma" (mā) is a redundant particle (ṣilah), and the meaning is that they are defeated and subdued. Scholars differed about what is meant by "there" (hunālika). One view is that they are the idols. The other view is that the meaning is the polytheists of Quraysh, those who were killed and captured at Badr. It was also said that "there" (hunālika) points to their places of death at Badr.

As for His saying, ﴿of the confederates﴾, meaning: of those who formed factions and gathered together against the prophets in denial.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 12:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Before them the people of Noah and ʿĀd denied, and Pharaoh, lord of the stakes﴾. This has already been explained.

As for His words: ﴿and Pharaoh, lord of the stakes (al-awtad)﴾, there are several opinions regarding "al-awtad" (the stakes). The first is that they are buildings (al-bunyan). A poet said:

(And indeed they lived in them in the most pleasant of lives, in the shade of a king whose stakes were firm.)

That is, the buildings. It was also said that al-awtad is the plural of watad (a stake, peg). When Pharaoh wished to kill a person, he would drive a stake into his hands and feet, four stakes in all, while the man lay on his back with his face toward the sky.

The third opinion is that al-awtad are the playgrounds (al-malaʿib) with ropes tied to stakes, and that Pharaoh had such things.

And Thamud and the people of Lot—this has already been explained. ʿAṭāʾ related from Ibn ʿAbbās that there is no prophet except that he will have a community (ummah) on the Day of Resurrection, apart from Lot, peace be upon him, for he will come alone. Some of them mentioned that the people of Lot were four hundred thousand houses, with ten persons in each house, and none of them was saved.

And His saying: ﴿And the companions of the Thicket﴾ means: the thicket (ghayḍah). And His saying: ﴿Those are the factions﴾ means: those who formed factions (taḥazzabū) against the prophets.

Almighty God's words: ﴿Each one of them did nothing but deny the messengers﴾, meaning: there was no people among them but that they denied the messengers. And His words: ﴿so My punishment was justly due﴾, meaning: My punishment became due upon them.

The Exalted said: ﴿And these only await a single shriek; there will be no pause for it.﴾ Here "the shriek" (al-sayha) is the blast in the Trumpet (nafkha fi al-sur).

As for His words ﴿mā lahā min fawāq﴾ (there will be no pause/return for it), it has been recited with both the accusative (naṣb) and the nominative (raf'). Some said: the two readings have one meaning. Others said: they differ. According to the accusative reading, it is from al-ifāqa (respite, recovering), and it has been said it means returning (muthanawiyya), and it is said it means return and delay. According to the nominative reading, it means "from waiting" (intiẓār). Al-fawāq, linguistically, is the interval between the two milkings (mā bayn al-ḥalbatayn), and the meaning is that the punishment will not give them respite, nor will it leave them waiting for that amount of time.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 16:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share (qitan) before the Day of Reckoning."﴾ Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: that is, our share (of) Paradise. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: qitan means our share of the punishment. They only said this in denial and mockery. The qitt (qitt) is the document in which the reward is written, and the qutut (qutut) are the books of rewards.

There is another view on the verse: when God, the Exalted, sent down His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand﴾ and ﴿As for him who is given his record in his left hand﴾, the polytheists heard this and said: "Our Lord, hasten to us our qitt," that is, our record.

As for His saying: ﴿before the Day of Reckoning﴾, it is clear. They only said it in denial and mockery.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Be patient over what they say﴾, meaning: be patient over what the disbelievers say.

And His saying: ﴿And remember Our servant Dawud﴾, he is Dawud son of Ishai, and this has been explained before. His saying: ﴿the one of strength (dha al-ayd)﴾, meaning: the one of strength. It is said: the one of strength in worship, and it is said: the one of strength in kingship.

As for His saying concerning worship: he would fast one day and break his fast one day, and he would stand in prayer for a sixth of the night, sleep for half of it, and stand in prayer for a third of it. And it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The most beloved fasting to Allah, the Exalted, is the fasting of Dawud, and the most beloved prayer to Allah is the prayer of Dawud."

And His saying: ﴿He is oft-returning (awwab)﴾, meaning: repentant (tawwab). It is also said: returning (raja'), from the verb āba, ya'ūbu, meaning he returned. The poet said:

(Every absent one returns, / but the one absent by death does not return)

It is also said: the meaning of awwab is that whenever he remembered his sin, he would seek forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 18:

The words of God, Exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, We subjected the mountains to glorify [Us] with him at evening﴾. Al-'ashi: the end of the day.

And His words: ﴿and at sunrise﴾. It is the time of ad-duha (the forenoon). It is related from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "I did not know the meaning of al-ishraq until Umm Hani, may Allah be pleased with her, informed me that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the duha prayer in her house, then said: 'This is the prayer of al-ishraq.'" And al-ishraq: it is when the sun shines until it reaches the height of its brightness.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿And the birds gathered together﴾, meaning: We subjected the birds, gathered together. And His words ﴿gathered together﴾ mean: assembled. And His words ﴿each one of them was oft-returning﴾ — the scholars have differed concerning the meaning of His words ﴿each one of them was oft-returning﴾. One of the two opinions is that its meaning is: each one of them was oft-returning to God, that is: glorifying Him.

The second opinion: each one of them was oft-returning, that is, to David, meaning: oft-returning along with him.

Here, the awwab (oft-returning) is the one who glorifies (tasbih), and tasbih (glorification of God) is the worship of the people of the heavens and the earth.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 20:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾, meaning: We made his kingdom strong. Mujahid said: He had four hundred thousand men guarding him, and it is well known that thirty-six thousand guarded him. And it is reported from some of them: forty thousand, mustala'mah, meaning: in arms, and he had put on his la'mah, meaning: his coat of mail and his weapons.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We gave him wisdom﴾, meaning: prophethood. It is also said: understanding of the religion. And it is said: understanding in judgment.

His saying: ﴿And decisive speech﴾ (fasl al-khitab). Concerning it there are several opinions:

The first: the evidence is incumbent upon the claimant, and the oath is incumbent upon the one who denies; this is fasl al-khitab. This is a famous and well-known opinion.

The second opinion: fasl al-khitab is the clear explanation that separates truth from falsehood.

The third opinion: its meaning is "amma ba'd" (and after that), related by al-Sha'bi. It was called "amma ba'd" fasl al-khitab because a person mentions God and praises Him, and then when he begins another speech he says: "Amma ba'd, such-and-such happened."

It is related in the story that a man came to Dawud, peace be upon him, and claimed that a certain person had seized cows from him. He summoned the accused, who denied it. Then [Dawud] saw in a dream that he was commanded to kill the accused, but he did not do it. He saw it a second and a third time, and was warned of punishment if he did not do it. So he summoned the accused and informed him that God, may He be exalted, had commanded him to kill him. He said: "Is it true?" He said: "Yes."

[The accused] said: "Will you kill me without proof?" [Dawud] said to him: "By God, I will surely carry out the command of God concerning you."

He said: "I was not going to be killed for this, but I had secretly killed this man's father and slain him," and he confessed to it. Dawud, peace be upon him, then killed him. When the Children of Israel saw that, they stood in awe of him with the utmost awe. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And We strengthened his kingdom﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 21:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And has the news of the disputants reached you?﴾ That is: the report of the disputants (al-khasm). They cited poetry where "news" (nabaʾ) is used in the sense of "report" (khabar):

"Indeed I stayed awake and my side did not close in sleep, out of anxiety over the great and grievous news."

The word khasm (disputant) applies to one, two, and a group. It has also been said that its meaning is: "possessor of a dispute" (dhū khaṣm), "two possessors of a dispute" (dhawā khaṣm), and "possessors of a dispute" (dhawū khaṣm). According to this, the term encompasses all of them.

And His words: ﴿When they climbed over the sanctuary wall﴾ That is: they ascended and went up. The meaning is that they entered from the side of the wall of the sanctuary (miḥrāb), not through the entrance by which people normally enter.

The majority of the exegetes agree that those who entered were two angels. It has been said that one of them was Jibrīl and the other Mīkāʾīl. The verb "climbed over" (tasawwarū) is stated in the plural form, because the plural includes two and more.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 22:

And His saying: ﴿When they entered upon Dawud, and he was startled by them﴾, that is: he feared them. The scholars differed concerning the cause of the fear. Some said: he feared them because they entered at a time other than the time of entry. It was also said: he feared them because they had entered from over the wall.

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Fear not"﴾, meaning: do not fear. ﴿Two adversaries, one of us has wronged the other﴾. If it is asked: how did he say ﴿one of us has wronged the other﴾ when neither of the two angels had wronged the other?

The answer to this is that its meaning is: "Consider two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other." This is one of the indirect forms of speech (ma'arid al-kalam), and it does not mean the actual establishment of one having wronged the other.

It was also said that its meaning is: they said, "What is your opinion regarding two adversaries, one of whom has wronged the other?" This is close to the first.

And His saying: ﴿So judge between us with truth﴾, that is: with justice.

And His saying: ﴿And do not exceed the due⁠﴾. It is said: ashatta yashuttu means when one oversteps (jara), and shatta yashuttu means when one goes far away (abada). The poet said:

(Shattat mazar al-'ashiqin, fa-asbahat ... 'asiran 'alayya talabuka ibnat Mikhram)

And 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'a said:
﴿Tashuttu ghadan dar jiranina ... wa-lil-dar ba'da ghadin abʻad⁠﴾

So the meaning of His saying ﴿and do not exceed⁠﴾ is: do not deviate. It has been read with a fatha on the ta', meaning: do not go far from the truth. And His saying ﴿and guide us to the even path﴾, that is: to the straight, correct and just way. And His saying ﴿and guide us﴾ means: and direct us.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is my brother; he has ninety-nine ewes﴾. The people of tafsir mentioned that the cause of the trial of Dawud, peace be upon him, was that he was tempted by the wife of Uriah son of Hanan. The reason for this was that Dawud, may Allah's blessings be upon him, used to divide his days: one day he would withdraw for worship, one day he would be with his wives, and one day he would sit in judgment with the Children of Israel, discussing with them and they discussing with him. One day he sat with the Children of Israel, discussing with them, and they discussed the temptation of women. Dawud privately resolved that if he were tested, he would seek protection.

In some tafsirs it is reported that Dawud, peace be upon him, saw his two companions from among the angels, and said to them: "What is the matter with you two with me?" They said: "We are protecting and guarding you." He reflected within himself that whatever he guarded against would happen through their protection, or whatever worship he performed would happen through their protection, and so he was not to be praised for that. Thereupon Allah the Exalted commanded the two angels to leave him alone for a day.

In some narratives it is reported that Allah the Exalted warned him one day, saying: "It is the day of your trial." In some of them it is reported that he heard the Children of Israel saying in their supplications: "O God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob," and he loved to be mentioned with them. He mentioned this to Allah the Exalted in his intimate supplication, and He said: "O Dawud, I tested them and they were patient." He said: "If You tested me, I would be patient." He said: "O Dawud, I will test you on such-and-such a day." When that day came, he entered his place of worship and devoted himself to worship. This third version is strange, and the well-known account is what we mentioned earlier.

They said: When that day came and he devoted himself to worship, he began to pray and recite the Torah and the Psalms, bending over their recitation. While he was in that state, suddenly a bird of gold fell near him. It is said that it was Iblis who appeared in the form of a bird, and its two wings were of pearl and chrysolite. He was impressed by the beauty of the bird and intended to take it, but it moved away from him, and he kept following it until he went to excess in pursuing it, to one of the houses of his neighbours. He saw a woman bathing, and her beauty and form impressed him, and he was tempted by her. When the woman sensed someone looking at her, she unbound her hair, and her hair covered her, so Dawud's temptation increased. He returned and asked about the woman, and it was said: "She is the wife of Uriah son of Hanan." At that time he was about to set out as a warrior to one of the frontier posts, so he wished that he would be killed and that he could marry her. Some mentioned that his sin was of this measure.

Some mentioned that he wrote to the commander of the army to place Uriah in front of the Ark, and whoever was placed in front of the Ark would either be killed or Allah would grant victory through his hands. When he was placed in front of the Ark, he was killed, and Dawud then married the woman after her waiting period had ended.

Masruq narrated from Ibn Mas'ud, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, that both of them said: the sin of Dawud was that he asked the man to step down from his wife. This is the saying of Ibn Mas'ud. As for the wording of Ibn 'Abbas: he asked that he might transfer her to him.

The people of tafsir said: Such a thing was permissible for them, but Allah the Exalted was not pleased with it for him, because it was out of desire for this world and an increase in women, and Allah the Exalted had already enriched him with what He had given him of other women.

Some mentioned that his sin was that he proposed to a woman when another had already proposed to her, so he entered upon the proposal of another, and this was forbidden in their law, just as it is forbidden in our law.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, this brother of mine has ninety-nine ewes﴾. Here "ewe" (na'jah) is a metaphor (kinayah) for a woman. The Arabs use "ewe" and "sheep" (shah) as a metaphor for a woman. The poet said:

(So I struck, when his eye was heedless of his sheep, and I hit the heart and spleen of it.)

The intended meaning of "sheep" here is a woman.

Ibn Mas'ud recited: "Ninety-nine ewes, female (unthā)." Some scholars said: the mention of "female" is for emphasis (ta'kid).

It has been narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Give the fixed shares to their people; what remains goes to the nearest male (rajul dhakar)." So his saying "male" is mentioned for emphasis.

It was also said: it is permissible to say "ninety-nine ewes" even if there is a male among them. So when he said "ninety-nine ewes, female," it became certain that there was no male among them.

As for His saying: ﴿And I have one ewe﴾, it is said in the exegesis that Uriah had one woman, and David had ninety-nine women, so this is what is meant by the sheep and the ewe.

As for His saying: ﴿So he said, "Entrust it to me"﴾, meaning: include it with me. It was also said: "Transfer it to me," and it was said: "Make me its guardian and surety for its affair."

As for His saying: ﴿and he overpowered me in speech﴾, meaning: he overcame me in the discourse, and dominated me in the speech, due to the strength of his kingship.

The real meaning is that the advantage was his because of my weakness in his hand, even though the right was with me. It is narrated from Mujahid who said: The Children of Israel spoke in David's presence that no day passes over the son of Adam without his committing a sin in it. David, peace be upon him, resolved that he would guard himself from sin, and he designated a day. When that day came, he withdrew into his place of worship, and began to pray, glorify God, and recite the Torah and the Psalms, and so he was tested with what he was tested with, as we have mentioned.

It is also narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: Whoever claims that David committed a forbidden act with that woman, I will flog him one hundred and sixty lashes, meaning double what is inflicted on a person for other offenses.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on Surah 38, verse 24:

His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿He said, "He has certainly wronged you by demanding your ewe be added to his ewes."﴾ Its meaning: he has certainly wronged you by his request that your ewe be added to his ewes. If it is asked: how could he say "he has certainly wronged you" merely on the basis of his statement, when he had not heard the words of his companion?

The answer to this: it is possible that he meant "he has certainly wronged you" on the basis of his statement alone, and his companion had not acknowledged that. And it is possible that he said: "If the matter is as you have mentioned, then he has wronged you by his request for your ewe to be added to his ewes." There is an ellipsis in the verse, and the omitted part is "by his request that your ewe be joined to his ewes." It is established from Ibn ʿAbbas that he had asked the husband of the woman to give up his wife to him; this was related by Saʿid ibn Jubayr from him.

His words: ﴿Indeed, many partners (khulaṭāʾ, sing. khalīṭ, "associates") oppress one another⦆ — that is, of the partners (shurakāʾ). It is said: "This is my khalīṭ," meaning my partner. His words: ﴿except those who have believed and done righteous deeds⦆ — meaning that they do not wrong one another. His words: ﴿and few are they⦆ — that is, "and few are these," and "mā" is extra (ṣilah).

His words: ﴿And David became certain that We had tried him⦆ — that is, David became certain that We had tested him, i.e., afflicted him and placed him in trial. It is read as "innamā fatanāhu" with a light pronunciation (takhfīf), meaning that the two angels were the ones who tested him.

His words: ﴿So he asked his Lord for forgiveness⦆ — that is, he sought forgiveness from his Lord. (﴿And fell down bowing⦆) — that is, prostrating; the prostration is expressed by "bowing" (rukūʿ), because each of them is a kind of bending.

His words: ﴿and turned in repentance⦆ — that is, he returned and repented. Mujāhid said: David remained prostrate for forty days, not raising his head. It is also said: he remained in prostration and wept until grass grew around his head.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that God, the Exalted, sent an angel to him after forty days, saying: "Raise your head." He did not raise it, so the angel said to him: "O servant, your first affair was a sin and its end is disobedience; raise your head, since your Lord has commanded you."

Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned that David, upon him be the blessings of God, did not drink water thereafter without mixing it with his tears, did not eat food without moistening it with his tears, and did not sleep on a bed without soaking it with his tears.

As for the ruling on prostration in this verse, some said it is a prostration of gratitude, and some said it is a prostration of obligation (ʿazīmah). Al-Shafiʿi, may God have mercy on him, related with his chain of transmission from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, may God be pleased with him, that he did not prostrate in "Surat Sad" and would say: "It is the repentance of a prophet."

In some tafsirs: when David, upon him be peace, said what he said, one of the two angels smiled to his companion, then they ascended to the sky. David then knew that they had intended him by that statement and that they were two angels sent from God, the Exalted; at that point he fell to the ground prostrating.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 25:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We forgave him that﴾. We forgave him his sin, that one. It is related from Abu Sulayman al-Darani that Allah the Exalted said: "O Dawud, I have forgiven your sin. As for the friendship that was between Me and you, it has passed away."

In the narrative: the wild beasts and the birds used to listen to his recitation and attend to it. When he did what he did, he would recite the Psalms (al-Zabur) after that, and neither the birds nor the wild beasts would attend to it. It is related that they said, meaning the wild beasts and the birds: "O Dawud, your sin has departed through the sweetness of your voice."

As for His words: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a nearness﴾, meaning closeness, ﴿and a good return﴾, meaning a good place of return and final abode. In some of the tafsir works: Dawud, peace be upon him, will be raised up with his sin inscribed upon his palm. When he sees it, he will say: "O Lord, I see my sin only as something that will destroy me." Then Allah the Exalted will say to him: "Come to Me, O Dawud." This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is a nearness and a good return﴾. And they recited poetry on the meaning of ruku' (bowing) as meaning sujud (prostration), in accordance with what we have explained:

(He fell upon his face bowing, and repented to Allah from every sin.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 26:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿O David, indeed We have made you a khalifah (successor, vicegerent) upon the earth﴾, meaning: a successor to those who came before, and it is said: "My khalifah." From this it is permissible to call the caliphs "khulafa' Allah" (successors of God).

As for His words: ﴿So judge between the people with truth﴾, meaning: with justice. And His words: ﴿And do not follow desire, for it will lead you astray from the way of Allah﴾, meaning: it will turn you away and divert you from the way of Allah.

As for His words: ﴿Indeed, those who go astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for having forgotten the Day of Account﴾, there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, and its meaning is: for them is a severe punishment on the Day of Account, because they forgot, i.e., they abandoned the command of Allah and were heedless of the Resurrection.

In the story: Allah the Exalted had sent down a chain from the sky, and it would be brought before David while the two litigants and the chain were in front of his assembly. He would order each of the two to take hold of the chain, and the one in the right would be able to reach it, while the one in the wrong would not be able to reach it. His awe increased among the Children of Israel because of this. Two men disputed over a necklace of pearls that one of them had deposited with the other, and the depositary denied it. The depositary went to a staff, hollowed it out, and placed the necklace inside it. When the two came before David, he ordered them to submit to judgment by the chain. The claimant went to the chain and said: "O Allah, if You know that I deposited this man a necklace of pearls and he did not return it to me, then let me reach the chain." Then he raised his hand and reached it. Then his companion came to the chain with the staff in his hand, and said to the claimant: "Hold this staff until I take the chain," and he took it from him. He said: "O Allah, if You know that I have returned it to him, then let me reach the chain." Then he raised his hand and reached the chain. David and the Children of Israel were perplexed by this.

Then Allah lifted the chain, and He commanded David, peace be upon him, to judge between the people by evidence (bayyinah) and oath (yamin). So the practice continued in this manner until the Hour arrives.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 27:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and whatever is between them in vain﴾. That is: in play. It was also said: without wisdom. And His words: ﴿That is the assumption of those who disbelieve﴾. This is evidence that God, exalted is He, punishes the disbelievers for the false assumption. And His words: ﴿So woe to those who disbelieve, from the Fire﴾. That is: from the Fire of Jahannam.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 28:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Or shall We treat those who believe﴾. Its meaning: "Shall We treat those who believe (and do righteous deeds) like those who cause corruption in the earth?" That is, "We do not treat them alike."

And His statement: ﴿Or shall We treat the God-fearing like the wicked?﴾ That is, "the believers like the disbelievers." It is also said: what is meant by "the God-fearing" here are the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). And it was said: they are the Banu Hashim and the Banu al-Muttalib. The "wicked" (fujjar) are the chieftains and leaders of the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 29:

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿A Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings﴾, meaning: this is a Book which We have sent down to you, full of blessings.

And His words: ﴿that they may ponder its verses﴾, meaning: that they may contemplate and reflect upon its verses. And His words: ﴿and that those of understanding may take heed﴾, meaning: that those possessed of intellects may be mindful. Al-Hasan (al-Basri) said regarding His words ﴿those of understanding (ulu al-albab)﴾: "He admonished them because He loved them."

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 30:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We gave to David Solomon. How excellent a servant! Indeed, he was one who often turned back (to Allah).﴾ Already explained.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 31:

His saying: ﴿When there were displayed before him, at evening, the poised, swift steeds﴾. That is, the swift horses (al-khayl al-jiyad). And al-ṣāfināt are the horses that stand on three legs, having bent one of their legs, and stand on the hoof-tip (al-sanbak).

It is also said: al-ṣāfin in the language is the one who stands. It has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever would love that people stand before him (yakūna al-nās lahu ṣufūnan), let him take his seat in the Fire," meaning standing. The poet said:

(He became accustomed to standing, so that it never ceases, as if it were, from standing on three legs, broken.)

As for His saying: ﴿al-jiyād﴾, that is, the swift. Ibrahim al-Taymi said: they were [twenty] horses that had wings. ʿIkrima said: twenty thousand horses that had wings. Some of them said: they were a thousand of the noble horses (al-khayl al-ʿitāq), that is, the generous ones. It is also said: God, exalted is He, had brought them out for him from the sea.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 32:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have preferred the love of good (khayr)﴾, meaning: I have given precedence to the love of good. As for "khayr," most exegetes hold that it refers to horses in this verse, and Ibn Mas'ud likewise read it with the lam (al-khayl).

It is related that Zayd al-Khayl al-Ta'i came as a delegation to the Prophet, and the Prophet said to him: "Who are you?" He said: "I am Zayd al-Khayl." He said: "Rather, you are Zayd al-Khayr."

The second view is that khayr here means worldly life (al-dunya), meaning: I preferred worldly life over the remembrance of my Lord, that is, the afternoon prayer (salat al-'asr).

His saying: ﴿until it was hidden behind the veil﴾, meaning: the sun was hidden behind the veil. He referred to the sun by a pronoun although it had not been mentioned, and we have already explained an example of this. It is said that something indicating the sun had already been mentioned, so the pronoun was correctly used for it, namely His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿when there were presented before him, at evening (al-'ashi), the swift-footed (steeds)﴾, and "al-'ashi" is only recognized through the sun.

As for the veil (al-hijab), it is said that it is Mount Qaf, and the sun sets behind it. It is also said that it is a mountain of green emerald, and the greenness of the sky comes from it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 33:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿Bring them back to me﴾, meaning: bring the horses back to me. And His saying: ﴿So he began to pass his hand over their shins and necks﴾. Most of the exegetes (mufassirun) held that what is meant by this is that he cut off their hamstrings (ʿarāqib) and their necks. This is related from Ibn ʿAbbas, al-Hasan and Qatadah, and it was adopted by al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj.

Al-Hasan said: he hamstrung them and struck their necks. Al-Zajjaj said: It is possible that God, exalted is He, permitted this to him at that time and has forbidden it to us in this time, and the Prophet of God would not have proceeded to do that if it were forbidden to him; and how would he seek forgiveness for a sin with a sin?!

And from Ibn ʿAbbas, in some narrations: that Sulayman, peace be upon him, began to wipe their hamstrings and necks with his hand and his garment out of compassion for them. This is a weak opinion, and this act does not befit what preceded it. The well-known view is the first opinion.

Al-Kalbi mentioned that the horses were a thousand, and he killed nine hundred of them and a hundred remained, and they are the origin of the noble horses that remained in the hands of people.

It is said: they were horses he had taken from the Amalekites, and they were presented to him; he became heedless of the afternoon prayer until the sun set, so he commanded that they be brought back to him, and he cut their hamstrings and struck their necks, because they had distracted him from the remembrance of God. It is also said: he slaughtered them with slaughter and gave their meat in charity, and slaughter was lawful in his law in that manner.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We did try Solomon﴾, meaning: We tested Solomon and afflicted him. It is also said: "We tried Solomon" means: We cast him into a trial (fitnah).

And His saying: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body; then he turned back in repentance﴾. Most of the exegetes held that the body which was placed upon Solomon's throne was Sakhr the jinn.

Al-Suddi said: "His name was Habiqiq." And it is reported from some of them that his name was Asaf, but the well-known one is the first, and it has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

As for his story, they claim that Sakhr was a rebellious devil (shaytan mārid) whom no one could overpower. So Allah, exalted is He, tested Solomon with him, stripped him of his kingdom, and this devil sat upon his throne judging among the people. The cause of that, as they claim, was that Solomon's kingdom was in his ring. Wahb said: "That ring was the one Allah, exalted is He, had put on Adam, peace be upon him, in Paradise, and it shone like the light of the sun. When Adam ate from the tree and disobeyed Allah, exalted is He, the ring was taken away."

Then Allah, exalted is He, sent it down to Solomon and bestowed his kingdom upon it. They said: The ring was square, having four sides. On one side was written: "I am Allah, who has not ceased to be." On the second side was written: "I am Allah, the Living, the Self-Subsisting." On the third side was written: "I am the Mighty; there is no mighty one but Me." On the fourth side was written: "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

It is also said that what was written upon it was the Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi). They said: When Solomon, peace be upon him, entered his bathing place, he would hand the ring to a female servant of his. He entered once and handed the ring to the servant, and Sakhr came in the form of Solomon and took the ring from the servant. Solomon came out seeking the ring, and she said: "You have already taken the ring from me once." So [Solomon] knew that Allah, exalted is He, had stripped him of his kingdom.

Solomon went wandering about the earth, and no one recognized him by his appearance. He would ask people for food, saying: "I am Solomon son of Dawud," but they would deny him, harm him, and claim that he was mad. It is related that once he asked food from a people and claimed that he was Solomon son of Dawud, so a man stood up and struck his head with a stick in his hand. Then they gave him a dry morsel of bread, and he carried the morsel to the bank of a river to soften it with water, for he was hungry and had not eaten any food for days, but the water carried the morsel away.

It is also said: he was on the shore of the sea, when a wave came and carried off the morsel, so he entered the sea in its pursuit until he feared drowning, and he returned, and the morsel returned. Then he coveted it again and went to take it, and the morsel went away, repeatedly in this manner. Solomon wept and humbled himself before Allah, exalted is He, so Allah, exalted is He, had mercy on him and restored his kingdom to him.

The cause of the restoration of his kingdom was that he passed by a people of fishermen, and he asked them for something to eat, and they gave him a dead fish. He split open its belly and found his ring inside it, so he put it on his finger, and his kingdom returned to him; the birds at once gathered over his head, and mankind, the jinn and the devils assembled before him.

As for the duration of the loss of his kingdom, it was [forty] days. As for the account of Sakhr the jinn: when he took the ring, having transformed into the form of Solomon, he went and sat upon his throne and began to carry out what Solomon used to carry out, except that Allah, exalted is He, prevented him from Solomon's wives. This is what is related from al-Hasan.

Others have mentioned that he would have intercourse with Solomon's wives during menstruation, and it is mentioned that he would have intercourse with them during menstruation and at other times. And Allah knows best.

There is a difference of opinion as to whether the ring remained with him or not. One of the two opinions is that he went and threw the ring into the sea.

The other opinion is that it remained with him, and the more famous opinion is preferable and better known.

Al-Naqqash mentioned in his tafsir that the Children of Israel denied the matter of Sakhr the jinn, because he was judging without right. So they went to Solomon's wives and said to them: "Do you deny anything in Solomon's affair?" They said: "Yes." At that point it occurred to their hearts that Solomon had been tested, that Allah, exalted is He, had stripped him of his kingdom, and that the person on the throne was a devil.

So they took the Torah and came around the throne and began to read it, and Sakhr flew to the highest part of the palace, then flew from the top of the palace, passed by, and fell into the sea.

It is also mentioned in the tafsir that when Allah, exalted is He, restored his kingdom to Solomon, He commanded the devils to seek Sakhr. They found him and brought him to Solomon, who bound him in iron, placed him in a chest, and cast him into the sea, where he remains until the Day of Resurrection.

As for the cause for which Allah tested Solomon, there are many opinions:

The first: that Allah, exalted is He, had commanded him not to marry a woman from outside the Children of Israel, but he disobeyed and married a woman from among others, so Allah, exalted is He, afflicted him with what we have mentioned.

The second opinion: that he married a woman, and the woman worshipped an idol in his house without Solomon being aware of it, so Allah, exalted is He, tested him for his heedlessness. This is a well-known opinion.

The third opinion: that he had a woman whom he loved intensely, and her brother disputed with a man before Solomon concerning something, and the woman asked Solomon to decide in favour of her brother. He said to her, "Yes," but did not do so, so Allah, exalted is He, tested him.

The fourth opinion: that he secluded himself from the people for three days and admitted no one, related by Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Allah, exalted is He, afflicted him with what we have mentioned, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: "O Solomon, I sent you and gave you this kingdom only so that you would do justice to the oppressed and be a helper to the weak against the strong, and I did not give you so that you would seclude yourself from the people."

The fifth opinion: that he once said, "By Allah, I will go around to my wives tonight, and he had three hundred wives and seven hundred concubines, and every one of them will conceive and bear a boy who will fight in the way of Allah." The king said to him: "Say, 'If Allah wills.'" But he did not say it, so none of them conceived except one woman, who bore half a human being, and Allah, exalted is He, afflicted him.

This is a report traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ). According to this opinion, the body placed upon his throne was his son. Some have mentioned that Solomon, peace be upon him, had a son, and he feared for him from the devils, so he entrusted him to the clouds to raise him; then he fell upon his throne dead. This is the meaning of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We placed upon his throne a body﴾. And Allah knows best.

The sixth opinion: what is related from al-Hasan, who said: he had intercourse with one of his wives during her menstruation, so Allah, exalted is He, afflicted him with what we have mentioned. And Allah knows best what occurred. There is no doubt that the verse indicates that Allah, exalted is He, seated another upon his throne and stripped him of something that had been his.

His saying: ﴿Then he turned back in repentance﴾, meaning: he returned to his kingdom.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 35:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿He said, "My Lord, forgive me and grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me."﴾ If someone says: How did he say, ﴿that will not belong to anyone after me﴾? Was this envy on his part toward others, so that no one else would attain what he attained?

The answer: The meaning of His saying, ﴿that will not belong to anyone after me﴾, is: it should not belong to anyone after me, in the sense that You would strip it from him and give it to another, just as You stripped my kingdom before and gave it to Sakhr... the report.

It is also said: He only asked for this so that his honour and special standing with Allah the Exalted would be made manifest. It is established by the narration of Abu Hurayrah from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "A devil confronted me last night, intending to spoil my prayer, but Allah the Exalted enabled me to overpower him. I seized him and wanted to tie him to a pillar so that you could all see him in the morning, but then I remembered the words of my brother Sulayman: ﴿My Lord, grant me a kingdom that will not belong to anyone after me﴾, so I let him go, and Allah sent him back frustrated and humiliated."

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed You are the Bestower﴾, meaning: the Giver.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 36:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿So We subjected the wind to him, flowing gently by his command, wherever he directed﴾. That is: gentle (layyinah). It is also said: rakhā’ means obedient, not disobedient.

His saying: ﴿wherever he directed (haythu aṣāb)﴾ means: wherever he intended (arāda). It is said that he would set out in the morning from Iliyā’ (Jerusalem), take his midday rest at Qazwīn, and spend the night at Bābil (Babylon). The Arabs say: "He aimed at the right thing (aṣāba al-ṣawāb) but missed the answer (fa-akhṭa’a al-jawāb)," meaning: he intended the right thing but got the answer wrong. The poet said:

(And other than her, whatever people had changed before her... she perished, and the needs of the heart aim at her.)

That is: they intend her.

And His saying: ﴿And the devils, every builder and diver﴾ — that is: We subjected to him the devils, every builder and diver among them. The subjugation of the wind and the devils to him came after his trial with what we have mentioned.

And His saying: ﴿And others bound together in shackles﴾ — meaning: fettered in chains. [The devil] would take them and bring them near to the devil, and bind them in iron, and fasten them in chains, and then place them in a chest of iron, and cast the chest into the bottom of the sea.

This is the commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 39:

On His words, the Exalted: ﴿This is Our gift﴾, there are several opinions. The first, and it is the most preferred, is that the kingdom is Our gift to you. ﴿So bestow [favours] or withhold﴾ means: give to whomever you wish. And His words ﴿or withhold﴾ mean: deny whomever you wish ﴿without reckoning﴾ means: without blame.

The second opinion: ﴿This is Our gift﴾ means: the subjugation of the devils. And His words ﴿So bestow or withhold﴾ mean: release whomever you wish, and restrain whomever you wish.

The third opinion: ﴿This is Our gift﴾ means: the women are Our gift. And His words ﴿So bestow or withhold﴾ mean: divorce whomever you wish, and keep whomever you wish ﴿without reckoning﴾ means: without blame.
The saying of God Most High: ﴿And indeed, for him with Us is nearness and a good place of return.﴾ That is, a good place of return.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 41:

The words of God Most High: ﴿And remember Our servant Job, when he called out to his Lord, "Satan has touched me with hardship and torment."﴾ It is also recited as "bi-nuṣbin wa ʿadhāb" with a fatḥah on the nūn and the ṣād. Al-naṣb and al-naṣīb have the same meaning, like al-ḥuznu and al-ḥuzn. It is said: "with nuṣb" refers to the body, and "ʿadhāb" refers to wealth.

We have already explained the story of Job and the affliction that befell him, and we mentioned the duration of his trial. It is said that he remained in the affliction for seven years, seven months, and seven days. Worms crawled over his body, and he was cast onto a dunghill, and his people harmed him to the utmost extent.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Strike with your foot﴾, meaning: strike the earth with your foot. It is said that he stamped the earth with a stamp, and a spring of [water] gushed forth. Allah the Exalted commanded him to wash himself in it, so he washed, and every ailment that was in his body departed. He walked forty steps, and Allah the Exalted commanded him to stamp the earth with his foot another time; he did so, and a spring gushed forth, sweeter and cooler than anything could be. Allah the Exalted commanded him to drink from it, and every ailment that was within him departed, and he became like the healthiest and most complete of men. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿This is a cool bath and a drink﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 43:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him his family﴾ — We have already explained that God, the Exalted, restored to him his family and his children whom He had destroyed, in their very persons, and we have stated other than this, but the first view (al-qawl al-awwal) is more akin to the apparent meaning of the Qur'an. It is said: the earth split open, so he saw his camels, cattle and sheep in their condition, and they came out to him; and he also saw his family and children as they were, and they came out to him.

As for His saying: ﴿and the like of them with them﴾ — it is said: [they were seven] sons and three daughters, so God the Exalted gave him the like of their number, and God returned them in their very persons.

As for His saying: ﴿as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding (ulu al-albab)﴾ — that is, for those of intellect (ulu al-'uqul).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 38, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And take in your hand a bundle [of grass], and strike with it and do not break your oath.﴾ That is: We said to him, "Take in your hand a bundle (ḍigh). The ḍigh is anything that fills the palm, of wood, grass, or other things."

His saying: ﴿So strike with it and do not break your oath.﴾ That is: strike with it your wife, and do not break your oath. The cause of his oath was that one day the woman brought him food that was more than she would usually bring him each day. So he accused her of dishonesty regarding herself, though she was innocent, and he swore that when he recovered from his illness he would strike her [one hundred] lashes.

It is also said that Iblis sat on the woman's path as a physician treating people. The woman passed by him and said, "I have a sick man, and I would like you to treat him." He said to her, "I will treat him, and I want nothing except that he say, when I have healed him, 'You have healed me.'" So she came to Ayyub and mentioned this to him. He recognised that it had been the accursed Iblis, so he became angry and swore the oath we have mentioned.

It is also said that she sold her two braids for two loaves of bread for his food. When Ayyub, peace be upon him, saw this, he became angry and swore. This opinion is strange (gharīb).

As for His saying: ﴿So strike with it and do not break your oath,﴾ that is: strike with the bundle which contains one hundred small twigs. ﴿And do not break your oath⁠﴾ means: do not leave off striking and thereby break it. Mujahid said: this ruling was specific to Ayyub. ʿAṭāʾ said: it applies to him and to people in general.

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, We found him patient. An excellent servant. Indeed, he was ever turning back (in repentance).﴾ That is: returning to obedience to Allah. In the narrative it is related that Ayyub was asked, "What was the hardest thing you encountered in your trial?" He said, "The gloating of the enemies."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 45:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And remember Our servants Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, possessors of strength and vision﴾. He singled out these three because Allah the Exalted tested them and they were patient. As for Abraham's trial, it was with the fire; Isaac's trial was with the sacrifice; and Jacob's trial was the loss of a son.

And His saying: ﴿possessors of strength and vision﴾ means: possessors of strength in obedience, and possessors of vision in knowledge. It was also said: possessors of outward strength and inward vision. The strength is the strength of the limbs, and the vision is the vision of the hearts. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts which are within the breasts﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 46:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We made them pure with a pure quality: the remembrance of the Abode﴾. It has been recited as "bi-khāliṣatin" without tanwīn. As for with tanwīn, its meaning is: with a pure quality (khallah khāliṣah), which is the remembrance of the Abode.

It has also been said that "the remembrance of the Abode" is an apposition (badal) for His saying ﴿khāliṣah﴾ according to this recitation. As for the recitation with the idafah (construct), its meaning is: We purified them with the best of what is in the Hereafter. This was related from Abu Zayd. Mujahid said: We purified them, through what we mentioned, by Paradise for them.

It is related from Malik ibn Dinar, who said Ibn 'Abbas said: We removed from their hearts the love of this world and its remembrance, and We purified them with the love of the Hereafter and its remembrance. And it is related from some of them: We purified them from calamities and defects, and made them remember the Abode of the Hereafter. The preferable view regarding His saying ﴿akhlaṣnāhum﴾ is: that is, We made them sincere (mukhlaṣīn) by what We have informed about them.
And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are with Us among the chosen and the excellent.﴾ Its meaning is apparent.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 38, verse 48:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And remember Isma'il and al-Yasa'﴾. Isma'il: he is Isma'il ibn Ibrahim. As for His saying ﴿al-Yasa'﴾: al-Yasa' is one of the prophets. It is said: al-Yasa' was the disciple of Ilyas, the Prophet, peace be upon him. When Allah raised Ilyas, peace be upon him, al-Yasa' succeeded him among his people. As for His saying ﴿and Dhu'l-Kifl﴾, we have already explained it. It is said: he is a man who took on (kafala) for a king that he would receive Paradise if he believed and obeyed Allah, may He be exalted. As for His saying ﴿and all are among the good ones﴾, its meaning is clear.
﴿This is a reminder. And indeed, for the righteous is an excellent place of return.﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 50:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Gardens of Eden, their doors thrown open for them﴾. That is: its doors.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿Reclining therein, they call therein for abundant fruit and drink﴾. That is: for the fruit of Paradise and its drink. He mentioned "abundant" (kathira) because what is in Paradise is abundant, since it never ends and its existence is vast.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 52:**

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And with them are those restricting their gaze, equal in age.﴾ That is, they restrict their glances to their husbands. His words ﴿equal in age﴾ mean: similar (amthal). It is also said: of the same age, with equal teeth. And from Mujahid: "equal in age, companionable, who neither rival one another nor bear hatred toward one another." It was also said: they do not become jealous. Yahya ibn Salam said: "They are daughters of thirty-three years." And from some of them: "equal in age" means they were created according to the measures of their husbands. And the poet recited regarding "those restricting their gaze":

(Of those who restrict their gaze, were a fine dust of the ant to rub against them, it would leave a mark upon them above the smooth skin.)
Almighty God's words: ﴿This is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning﴾. That is: this which We have told you of is what you were promised for the Day of Reckoning.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, this is Our provision; it has no end.﴾ "Without end" means without cessation. The meaning of His saying ﴿Our provision﴾ is Our giving.

Almost-verbatim translation with the required conventions:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿This is so. And indeed, for the transgressors is an evil final return.﴾ That is: an abode of return. And what is meant by "the transgressors" is the disbelievers.

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on surah 38, verse 56:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Hell, which they will enter, and it is an evil resting place.﴾ That is, they will enter it. It is also said: they will suffer its heat. And His saying: ﴿So wretched is the resting place﴾ means: wretched is what they prepared for themselves, and it is said: wretched is the bed.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 57:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This! So let them taste it: boiling water and ghassaq.﴾ It is said that there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, and its meaning is: "This is boiling water and ghassaq, so let them taste it." As for the meaning of ḥamīm (boiling water), we have already explained it: it is water that is heated to the utmost degree of heat. As for ghassaq, it is the pus that flows from their skins. It is reported from al-Suddi that he said: "It is the tears that flow from their eyes." Some of them related from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the zamharir (extreme cold) which burns them with its cold. Al-Naqqash related that ghassaq is "the stinking" in Turkish, which was then Arabized. It has been read with tashdid (doubling of the ghayn) and with takhfif (without doubling). Some of them said: there is no difference between the two in meaning, while others distinguished between them by some of the aspects we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 58:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And other punishments of similar kind, in pairs﴾. It is also read: "wa-ākharu" (and another). So His saying ﴿wa-ākharu﴾ (and other) with the short vowel covers the plural, and His saying ﴿wa-ākharu﴾ with the long vowel (ākharu, as "āḫar" in the singular) covers the one.

His saying ﴿min shakslihi﴾ (of similar kind) means: like it. His saying ﴿azwāj﴾ (pairs) means: categories (aṣnāf). It is also said: types (anwāʿ). The poet said:

(When they were clothed in every kind of strike, red and green, like the greenness of herbs.)

The meaning of the verse is that for the people of the Fire there are other types of punishment, of the same kind as what has been mentioned before, meaning: in its severity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 59:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿This is a troop rushing in with you﴾, meaning: a troop rushing in with you after the first troop. Al-iqtiham (rushing in, entering) is entry. Scholars differed regarding the first troop and the second troop.

As for one of the two opinions: the first troop are the Children of Israel, and the second troop are the Children of Adam. It is also said: the first troop are the leaders and commanders, and the second troop are the followers.

His saying: ﴿No welcome to them﴾. Al-rahb (marhaban) is spaciousness. The saying of the speaker, "No welcome to so-and-so" (la marhaban bi-fulan), means: may his place not be spacious for him, i.e., may he not be given room. The poet said:

(When you come to his gate, he says "Marhaban!" ... "Ahlan and marhaban, your visit is not unwelcome!")

His saying: ﴿Indeed they will burn in the Fire﴾, meaning: they will enter the Fire along with you.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 60:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿They will say, "Rather, you! There is no welcome for you."﴾ Meaning: the followers said to the leaders, "Rather, you! There is no welcome for you."

And His words: ﴿You brought it upon us﴾ meaning: you brought this punishment upon us by your calling us to misguidance and disbelief. And His words: ﴿Wretched is the abode﴾ meaning: wretched is the abode of settlement, the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 61:

And His Exalted saying: ﴿They will say, "Our Lord, whoever brought this upon us, increase him in doubled punishment in the Fire."﴾ That is: the followers say, "Our Lord, who brought this upon us?" And His saying: ﴿So increase him in doubled punishment in the Fire.﴾ That is: double the punishment upon him in the Fire.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 62:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they will say, "What is [wrong] with us that we do not see men whom we used to count among the evil?"﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Abu Jahl and his kind will say when they enter the Fire: "Where is Bilal? Where is 'Ammar? Where is Khabbab? And so-and-so and so-and-so?"

It is related from some of them that he said: The people of the Fire say this when they miss the people of Paradise.

And His saying: ﴿We used to count them among the evil﴾ — some of them said: among the vile (al-aradhil). And some of them said: We used to count them among the worst of our people, because they had abandoned the religion of their forefathers.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Did We take them as objects of ridicule?﴾ That is: "We used to ridicule them." It is also recited as "Atakhadhnahum sukhriyyan" (أتخذناهم سخريا) in the interrogative form. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The first recitation is preferable, because they will have known the reality of matters on the Day of Resurrection, so a question from them is not conceivable. Al-Farra' said: The alif in His saying ﴿Did We take them…﴾ is the alif of reproach and astonishment, and the Arabs mention this kind of alif in the manner of reproach and astonishment.

And His saying: ﴿Or have the eyes turned away from them?﴾ That is: the eyes have inclined away from them. Its meaning is: they are with us in the Fire, and we do not see them.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, that is true: the dispute of the people of the Fire﴾. That is, the mutual exchange of speech among them is like that of disputants.

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: I am only a warner, and there is no god except Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ That is: I am the messenger who warns, and Allah is the One, the Subduer (al-Qahir) of His servants by what He wills.

Allah's saying, ﴿The Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Mighty, the Forgiving﴾: that is, the Invincible in His dominion, the One who forgives the sins of His servants.

Almost all of the commentary words here are plain Arabic; the only technical terms are "Tafsir" (already in title) and none requiring gloss beyond that. Translating now.

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: It is a momentous tidings﴾. That is, the Qur'an is a momentous tidings. It was also said: it is of great importance. Some of them interpreted "the momentous tidings" as the Resurrection,
"And His saying: ﴿You turn away from it﴾, meaning: heedless of it, and neglecting it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 69:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they were disputing﴾. Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) went to the view that what is meant by "the Exalted Assembly" is the angels, and this is the statement of Ibn 'Abbas and others.

And His words: ﴿when they were disputing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, said: it is their saying to Allah the Exalted regarding the matter of Adam: ﴿Will You place in it one who will cause corruption therein and shed blood?﴾ to the end of the verse.

As for what has been related (al-ma'thur) from the Prophet concerning the verse, it is what Mu'adh ibn Jabal, may Allah be pleased with him, related: "The Prophet delayed coming to us one morning until we nearly saw the sun rising. Then he came out quickly, and the call to prayer was given, and he prayed two rak'ahs briefly, then said: Do you know why I was delayed from you? We said: No. He said: I got up during the night, performed ablution, and prayed what Allah willed. Then I dozed and became deeply asleep, and behold, my Lord was in the best of forms.

He said: O Muhammad. I said: At your service.

He said: Do you know what the Exalted Assembly are disputing about? I said: No.

So He placed His palm between my shoulders until I felt the coolness of His fingertips upon my chest, and everything was made clear to me, and I recognised it.

Then He said to me: O Muhammad, do you know what the Exalted Assembly are disputing about?

I said: Yes, concerning the expiations (kaffarat). He said: What are they? I said: Walking on foot to the congregations, perfecting the ablution in disliked conditions, and sitting in the mosques after the prayer.

He said: And about what else?

I said: About giving food, speaking gently, and praying at night while people are asleep.

Then He said to me: Ask, O Muhammad.

I said: I ask You to do good deeds, to abandon evil deeds, to love the poor, that You forgive me and have mercy on me, and I ask You for Your love, and the love of those who love You, and the love of deeds that bring me closer to Your love.

Then the Prophet said: "Indeed these are true, so study them and teach them." Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: This is a sound hadith, and this report has been related by other routes, and in some of them the sleep is not mentioned, and this narration is the most sound, and Allah knows best."

There is another view regarding the verse: that the Exalted Assembly are the nobles of Quraysh, and their disputing was that some of them said: the angels are the daughters of Allah, and others said otherwise; this is their disputing. The first view is more sound.

The disputing of the angels is their discourse about these deeds, and the measure of reward for them, and the excelling of some deeds over others in reward.
Allah's words: ﴿It is only revealed to me that I am but a clear warner﴾. That is: only this is revealed to me, that I am but a clear warner.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed I am going to create a human being from clay."﴾ He means: Adam, upon whom be the blessings of Allah.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 72:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿So when I have fashioned him﴾ means: I have gathered his creation and perfected him.

And His saying: ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit, so fall down to him in prostration﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 38, verse 75:

The words of God Most High: ﴿He said, "O Iblis, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands?"﴾ have already been explained.

As for His words ﴿Have you become arrogant?﴾, meaning: have you exalted yourself. And His words ﴿Or were you among the haughty?﴾, meaning: were you among the people who are arrogant. Ibn 'Abbas said: Iblis was among the noble angels, and he was the keeper of the Gardens (khazin al-jinan) and the trustee of the lowest heaven (amin al-sama' al-dunya). So he was impressed with himself, and he saw that he had a virtue over others. When God Most High commanded him to prostrate to Adam, he refused because of that which was in his soul.

Almighty God says: ﴿He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."﴾ Iblis said this only because he [thought] that fire is superior to clay. But it was not as he thought; rather, superiority belongs to the one whom God grants superiority.
Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said, "Then get out of it, for indeed you are accursed."﴾ That is, marjum (stoned, pelted), and the marjum is the one who is driven away with the curse.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 78:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Recompense﴾. That is: until the Day of Resurrection. It has also been said: until the Day of Reckoning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 79:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are resurrected."﴾ That is: give me respite.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 80–81:

And His saying: ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those reprieved until the Day of the appointed time."﴾ That is, until the blowing of the Horn (al-ṣūr), and it is the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ūlā). The accursed one wanted to be given respite until the second blast, so that he would escape death. Allah, exalted is He, knew his intention, so He did not grant him his wish; He gave him respite until the blowing into the Horn for the first blast, and the creatures die, so he dies along with them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 80–81:

And His saying: ﴿He said, "Indeed, you are among those reprieved until the Day of the appointed time."﴾ That is, until the blowing of the Horn (al-ṣūr), and it is the first blast (al-nafkhah al-ūlā). The accursed one wanted to be given respite until the second blast, so that he would escape death. Allah, exalted is He, knew his intention, so He did not grant him his wish; He gave him respite until the blowing into the Horn for the first blast, and the creatures die, so he dies along with them.
"The words of the Exalted: ﴿He said, 'By Your might, I will surely mislead them all'﴾, that is: I will surely lead them astray, all of them."
"And His Exalted saying: ﴿Except Your sincere servants among them﴾, i.e., those whom You have purified for Yourself."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 84:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said: "Then the truth, and the truth I say"﴾. It was also read: "fa-al-haqqa wa-al-haqqa aqulu" (with the first and second words in the accusative). As for the reading with the accusative in both places, it has two meanings:

The first: "Truth, truth I say" (i.e., I say the truth, truth).

The second meaning: the first is in the accusative by way of "I say the truth," and the second is in the accusative by way of incitement (al-ighra', i.e., a warning or urging to hold fast), as if he said: "Hold fast to the truth." This was mentioned by al-Azhari (d. 370 AH).

As for the second reading, His saying ﴿fa-al-haqq﴾ means: "I am the truth." It was also said: "From Me is the truth." And His saying ﴿wa-al-haqq﴾ means: "I say the truth."
"And His saying: ﴿I will surely fill Hell with you and with those among them who follow you, all together﴾ — its meaning is apparent."

Al-Sam'ani's words on the verse: ﴿Say: I do not ask you any wage for it﴾, that is, no reward (ajr). And His words ﴿nor am I of those who pretend (al-mutakallifin)﴾, that is: I did not say what I have said of my own accord. Whoever says something of his own accord has indeed taken it upon himself (takallafa lahu).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 38, verse 87:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿It is nothing but a reminder to the worlds﴾. That is: it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds, that is: an honour (sharaf) for the worlds, a reminder (tadhkir) to them.

"His word, exalted is He: ﴿And you will surely know its news after a while﴾. That is, the Day of Resurrection. It is also said: after death. And it was said: the Day of Badr. Al-Hasan al-Basri used to say: "O son of Adam, at death the news comes to you."
